verdict.rationale: The evidence documents official web and mobile SDKs (RealtimeKit UI and Core SDK), a server-controlled HTTPS SFU API with signaling on your own backend, and per-role participant permissions. These are pieces of the flow, but nothing explicitly documents creating a session from the server, minting a scoped join token, or a short end-to-end quickstart. missing for 10: documented server-side session/meeting creation endpoint, scoped join-token minting, client connect-with-token step in the SDK, a short documented end-to-end flow, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can create a session from my server, mint a scoped join token, and connect a client with the official SDK in a short documented flow

citations.quote: Use prebuilt meeting UI and SDKs for web and mobile.
Use [RealtimeKit Core SDK](/realtime/realtimekit/humans/core/) to build every screen and interaction yourself.
Use the Realtime SFU API to control which endpoints publish or receive audio, video, and data.
Your signaling backend can run on Workers, in a container, or on your existing infrastructure.
Give hosts, speakers, and attendees different permissions for media, moderation, and in-meeting features.
